answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The tundra multiplier is published, charged in sable, and timber lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4260 identities would post 1081 proofs and burn roughly 81 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
